reviews.en: Why is being resilient connected with bouncing back?
Elastic; able to recover from difficulty.
The key is recovery after being affected, not never being affected.
The Latin source of resilient is connected with jumping or springing back. Picture a branch that returns to its shape after being bent.
The word first concerned returning to a position, then materials recovering after pressure, and later people recovering from difficulty. The metaphor does not mean a person never feels hurt or sad.
The team remained resilient after the setback.
See how the adjective becomes a noun meaning resilience.
Compare being strong with being able to recover.
Being able to recover after being affected.
Bouncing back emphasizes recovery, rather than never being affected.
Why is resilience more than merely enduring?
Resilience; the capacity to recover or spring back.
Use the image of springing back to connect material elasticity with human recovery.
Resilience is historically connected with Latin resilire, meaning to spring back; re- contributes the idea of returning.
Think of resilience as the name of an ability. Use the adjective resilient to describe a person or material with that ability.
The community showed resilience after the storm.
Switch to the adjective and see how it describes people and materials.
Which word names the capacity to recover?
Resilience is a noun; resilient is an adjective.
Why is the word for an asset connected with enough?
An asset; a valuable person or thing.
Understand assets through the idea of property sufficient to pay obligations.

Assets is connected with Old French assez, meaning enough. Early legal uses concerned property sufficient to meet debts and other obligations, later developing into property and assets more generally.
The singular asset was later formed from assets. It can also mean a useful person or advantage, such as valuable experience.
Her experience is a valuable asset to the team.
Another business word, not a shared root: explore a different history of equity.
Compare the contexts in which assets and capital are used.
What does asset mean in Her experience is an asset?
Money she has in a bank account.
An asset can be a useful ability or advantage, not only financial property.
Why can equity mean both fairness and an ownership interest?
Fairness; equity in law; an ownership or financial interest.
A useful connection is the idea of rights that someone ought fairly to enjoy.
Equity can be traced through French to Latin forms associated with equality and fairness. Equitable principles in law are an important branch of its meaning.
It also came to describe rights that someone properly holds. In finance, equity and equities concern ownership interests and shares. Context matters: equity does not always mean shares.
The discussion focused on equity in education.
Trace the shared linguistic idea of equality and fairness.
Compare equity with assets in business contexts; they are not synonyms.
How should equity in education be understood?
Ownership of shares in education businesses.
The context is education, so equity means fairness rather than company shares.
How did writing underneath become underwriting insurance or securities?
To underwrite insurance or securities; to provide financial support.
Remember accepting responsibility through the image of signing underneath a document.
Underwrite was connected with writing beneath a document and signing agreement. This literal image helps connect the word with its insurance meaning.

Signing a marine insurance document came to signify accepting responsibility for an agreed loss. Underwrite developed insurance and financial-guarantee senses, and is also used for securities underwriting. The intended sense depends on context.
The insurer agreed to underwrite the risk.
See what the person or organization performing this role is called.
Another word connected with writing one's name underneath.
What does signing underneath mainly represent in this history?
Agreeing and accepting the corresponding responsibility.
Erasing the bottom of a document.
Signing became associated with agreement and responsibility, leading to later insurance uses.
Is mort in mortgage really connected with death?
A mortgage loan; to secure a loan against real property.
Its older form literally suggests a dead pledge, not having to repay for the rest of one's life.
Mortgage comes from Old French mort, dead, and gage, a pledge or security. These are its historical components.
A traditional explanation is that repayment or default brings the pledge arrangement to an end. Think of the end of the security arrangement, not the borrower's lifespan.
They applied for a mortgage to buy a home.
A mortgage and a general loan do not have exactly the same scope.
Move from borrowing to bearing risk: this is a topic connection, not a shared root.
Which claim cannot be inferred from this etymology of mortgage?
The loan must be repaid until the borrower dies.
Dead describes the pledge in the older expression, not the borrower's lifespan.
Why does the history of company involve bread?
A company; a group of people; companionship.
Connect people sharing bread with companions, groups, and working together.
Company came through Old French. Its earlier Latin source combines ideas of together and bread, referring to people sharing a meal.
From companions and people acting together to a business group, companionship and a company become connected meanings. This does not imply that modern companies originally sold bread.
Another word connected with companionship and sharing.
From a company to capital: a thematic rather than a root connection.
What does company mean in I enjoy your company?
Company also means companionship; the sentence is not discussing a business.
Why can capital mean a chief city, a large letter, and business wealth?
A capital city; capital funds; an uppercase letter; principal.
Head and chief provide a memory connection between these branches.
Capital is connected with Latin caput, head, and developed ideas of being chief or principal. Capital letters occur at the starts of sentences or names; a capital city is the main seat of government.

The financial sense developed through principal property, the principal sum, and wealth used in business. The meanings arose along related historical branches, rather than from a single mechanical formula.
Start the sentence with a capital letter.
From capital to people or systems associated with it.
Compare capital and assets without treating them as synonyms.
This is a writing context, not a financial one.
How can a concession be both a compromise and a special right?
Think of yielding or allowing in two different contexts.
In negotiation, a concession is something one side gives up. In business, it may be a granted operating right. Both connect with giving, allowing, or yielding.
Con- in this word should not mechanically be read as together. The historical material below follows concession itself rather than repeating a whole root family's story.
Both sides made concessions to reach an agreement.
Return to the verb and understand the act of acknowledging or yielding.
Follow the ced/cess connection and see how retreating enters economic language.
What does make a concession usually mean in negotiations?
Make a compromise or yield a point.
It means yielding a condition or position, not setting out or travelling.
What is the difference between process and procedure?
How something unfolds is not the same as the prescribed steps for doing it.
Procedure is historically connected with going forward. In modern usage, focus on a method, set of steps, or formalities for handling a matter.
Process can emphasize how an activity or change unfolds; procedure often means a prescribed sequence of steps. A shared ced/cess connection does not make them interchangeable.
One emphasizes a process; the other often emphasizes prescribed steps.
See how to express continuing or proceeding.
A set of safety steps to follow.
Procedure here means an operating procedure that must be followed.
Success, successful, or successfully: which belongs in the sentence?
Their meanings connect, but one is a noun, one an adjective, and one an adverb.
Successful combines success with -ful to describe something effective or successful. Adding -ly gives successfully, which modifies an action.
First decide whether you are describing a quality or how an action was completed, then choose the form.
Return to the noun and see success used as a concept.
Move from adjective to adverb for a more precise sentence.
Which form completes The project was _____?
An adjective is needed here to describe the project's state.
Why can photograph be remembered as recording with light?
Photo- relates to light, while -graph relates to recording or drawing.
Photograph provides a clear word-formation example: light helps create an image, and recording or depicting is the result. Combining the parts gives a memorable picture.
Continue to photographer and photographic, noticing how suffixes turn a photograph into a person who photographs or an adjective about photography.
She took a photograph of the lake.
-er points to the person who does the photography.
Notice how an adjective describes techniques or works.
What does photo- chiefly suggest in photograph?
Photo- is associated with light; tele- commonly supplies the idea of distance.
How is sound from far away built into telephone?
Tele- contributes distance and -phone contributes sound.
Telephone combines distance and sound, expressing the purpose of transmitting sound over a distance.
Now compare microphone: the ending still relates to sound, but the beginning changes. Comparing the parts offers more than memorizing one translation.
They share a sound-related element but use different prefixes.
Move from a device to speech sounds themselves.
What does tele- relate to in telephone?
It contributes the idea of distance; the other element supplies sound.
How do bio- and -logy form the name of a subject?
Connect life with study so that biology becomes more than a string of letters.
As a learning analysis of the modern word, bio- suggests life and -logy commonly appears in names of fields of study.
This helps explain word formation; it does not mean every word ending in -logy has exactly the same kind of study meaning. Compare biological to see how the ending changes word class.
From a subject's name to an adjective meaning biological.
It also concerns life, but -graphy points to writing or recording rather than the same academic subject.
What does bio- suggest in biology?
Bio- is commonly associated with life.
How does forming again help us understand reform?
Re- and form are a starting point, but reform does not mean simply repeating old practices.
Reform is connected with Latin, French, and English forms meaning to form again or reshape. It can be a noun or a verb in modern English.
In institutional and procedural contexts, it often means improving or changing a system. Roots provide a clue, while the sentence determines the intended meaning.
The team proposed reforms to the process.
Both contain form, but their prefixes give different emphases.
Return to the act or result of forming.
What does reform usually mean in an institutional context?
It emphasizes changing existing arrangements, not repeating them unchanged.
Did apple always mean only the apple we know today?
Start with a familiar fruit and discover a broader older meaning.
Apple developed from Old English æppel through Middle English appel. Its earlier scope was broader and could include certain fruits generally; in ordinary modern usage it mainly means an apple.
There are three apples in the bowl.
Move from a particular fruit to the general word fruit.
Extend apple juice to other expressions for drinks.
From an apple tree, explore words for trees and fruit.
How do you say one apple?
A or an depends on the initial sound of the following word. Apple begins with a vowel sound, so use an.
Water is a substance, but can it also mean giving water to plants?
The spelling stays the same, but using the word as a verb changes the sentence's meaning.
Water is usually uncountable when it names the substance. To specify an amount, say a glass of water or two bottles of water.
As a verb, water can mean giving water to plants or land. Check its role in the sentence instead of always reading it as the noun.
I filled the bottle with water.
Connect the substance water with the action of drinking.
How do you count bottles of water?
What receives the water in water the plants?
What does Please water the plants mean?
Please give water to the plants.
Please remove the water beside the plants.
Water is a verb here and means giving water to the plants.
Does book a room mean reading in a room?
noun: a book; verb: to reserve.
Book can mean a written volume or the act of making a reservation.
As a noun, book can name a written volume. As a verb, it can mean reserving a seat, room, or service. Book a room means reserving accommodation, not reading in it.
In some business contexts, books means accounting records. First identify the word class and its surrounding words.
I read a book on the train.
Connect a book with the activity of reading.
Compare book and reserve in reservation contexts.
Which words help when borrowing or returning books?
What does booked mean in I booked a table?
Put a book on the table.
Reserved a table at a restaurant.
Book a table is a restaurant reservation expression; book is a verb here.
Why are logs raised off the floor of a fireplace?
noun: an andiron, a metal support for firewood.
It is neither the wood nor the fireplace: an andiron is a metal support placed inside a fireplace to hold logs.
Andirons are usually used in pairs, with logs laid across them. The space underneath lets air circulate and helps the wood burn.
The logs rest on a pair of andirons.
Where is it used? Start with fireplace.
Here logs means pieces of wood for fuel, not computer records.
Another name for the same fireplace tool
This names the same object, not an animal.
A metal support holding logs in a fireplace.
Wood placed in a fireplace to burn.
An andiron is the support; a log is the piece of fuelwood.
How can yielding something become granting a right?
From a compromise to a concession, then compare the economic sense of retreating.
Connect a photograph with a photographer, photographic, and photocopy.
Distinguish moving forward, an unfolding process, and prescribed steps.
Four business words connected by topic rather than a shared root.
An older word form survives, while its meaning becomes focused on the familiar apple.
Used for apples and sometimes for fruit more generally.
Closer to the modern spelling and pronunciation.
Usually names the apple in everyday use; further meanings occur in fixed expressions.
Why do we say an apple?
Apple begins with a vowel sound. For one, say an apple; for more than one, use apples.
I put an apple and two pears in the bag.
An informal expression for someone whose bad behaviour negatively affects a group. This does not make apple alone an ordinary word for a person.
One bad apple should not define the whole team.
An idiom for someone especially cherished or loved.
His granddaughter is the apple of his eye.
Comparing things that differ in nature and cannot appropriately be compared directly.
Those two prices cover different services; we are comparing apples and oranges.
noun: an apple; an apple tree, depending on context.
Would you like apple juice or water?
From a noun to an action
Use some water or much water for the substance. Count it with units such as glasses and bottles. In a restaurant, a water can mean a serving, with the unit left unstated.
Please bring two glasses of water.
Water the plants means giving water to plants, not water belonging to them.
Could you water the plants this evening?
noun: water, usually uncountable; a body of water.
verb: to water; to supply with water.
She waters the flowers before breakfast.
A different use of a familiar word
Book is normally countable when it means a written volume: a book, or several books.
These books belong to the library.
Book a room, a ticket, or a seat
As a verb, book means arranging or reserving in advance. Its past form is booked and its -ing form is booking.
We booked a room for Friday.
In financial contexts, books can mean account books or accounting records, not books for general reading.
The accountant checked the books carefully.
noun: a book; a notebook; accounting books.
verb: to reserve; to make an appointment.
Please book a table for four.
Noun and verb meanings of book
First see what the object is.
noun: an andiron, a metal support for logs in an open fireplace, usually used in pairs.
Metal supports placed in a fireplace to hold logs.
A noun label, not part of the definition.
Physical supports or stands, not the verb meaning to support.
Pieces of wood for fuel, not computer logs.
Use andiron for one and andirons for a pair.
This is a countable noun for an object. Because the supports are often paired, a pair of andirons is a common description.
Why does dog appear in the source material?

Firedog, dog-iron, and sometimes dog can name this fireplace support. This is a specialized sense for an object, not a claim that an andiron is an animal. Do not interchange them when speaking of pets.
An andiron is also called a firedog.
We placed the wood on the andirons.
Connect the word with the actual object.
The metal supports lift logs off the fireplace floor so air can circulate underneath. Their upright fronts also help stop logs rolling out. They are usually used as a pair.
Two metal andirons hold logs across them inside a fireplace, leaving space underneath for ventilation.
The metal supports are andirons; the pieces of wood across them are logs.
A long, slightly curved fruit with a peel that can be removed and soft flesh inside. In familiar varieties, the peel becomes yellow and the flesh sweet as the fruit ripens.
A banana is one fruit; banana peel is its outer skin.
She peeled a banana before eating it.
Independently written learning explanation and original example sentences.
In botanical contexts, banana can also name the plant: a large herbaceous plant of tropical or subtropical regions. Herbs in the definition means herbaceous plants, not culinary seasoning.
A usually rounded fruit with red, green, or yellow skin, flesh inside, and a core containing seeds.
With an initial capital, Apple may be the company name; check the context.
I cut the apple into small pieces.
Orange: the fruit or the colour
As a noun, orange can name a citrus fruit with an outer peel and flesh divided into segments. It also names the colour orange.
An orange is a fruit; an orange bag is a bag of that colour.
She squeezed an orange to make juice.
A juicy fruit with white or pale flesh. Some varieties narrow near the stem and have a rounded base.
The pear is sweet and juicy.
A citrus fruit whose familiar varieties have yellow skin when ripe and sour juice, often used for flavouring or drinks.
Add a little lemon juice to the water.
A small juicy berry growing in clusters, often green or purple. Grapes may be eaten fresh or made into raisins or wine.
She washed a bunch of grapes.
A fruit usually red when ripe, with a sweet-tart flavour and many small grainlike structures on its surface.
There are fresh strawberries in the bowl.
A tropical fruit with a firm, scaly outer skin, a tuft of leaves at the top, and juicy, sweet-tart flesh.
We cut the pineapple into slices.
A large melon with a thick rind and very watery flesh. Familiar varieties have red flesh, though other colours occur.
They shared a watermelon on a hot day.
A fruit with flesh surrounding a hard stone. Familiar varieties have fine fuzz on their skin and become soft and juicy when ripe.
The peach has a hard stone inside.
A usually small, rounded stone fruit on a slender stalk. Familiar ripe varieties are red or dark red.
There are cherries on the cake.
A tropical stone fruit with relatively smooth skin, usually yellow or orange flesh when ripe, and a large stone in the middle.
She added pieces of mango to the salad.
A mammal commonly kept by people, usually with four legs, fur, and a tail. Dogs can be companions or trained to help with work.
As a verb, dog can mean persistently following or troubling someone; that is not the animal-name sense.
The dog waited beside the door.
A common feline mammal with an agile body, whiskers, and retractable claws, often kept as a pet.
The cat slept on the sofa.
A mammal with long ears, a short tail, and strong hind legs, usually feeding on plants and moving quickly by hopping.
The rabbit moved its long ears.
A large hoofed mammal with a mane along its neck, historically used for riding, pulling vehicles, and transport.
They rode horses along the path.
A ruminant commonly raised by people. Many breeds grow wool that can be shorn, and they mainly feed on plants.
Sheep has the same form in the singular and plural.
A hoofed ruminant, often with horns and sometimes a beard, capable of moving on relatively steep ground.
A goat stood on the rocks.
A large cat whose familiar appearance is orange-yellow fur with dark stripes. Tigers feed on other animals.
The tiger walked through the forest.
A large cat that commonly lives in groups; adult males usually have a conspicuous mane.
The male lion has a thick mane.
Hoofed mammals, usually with slender legs. In many species, males have antlers that are periodically shed and regrown.
Deer has the same form in the singular and plural.
We saw two deer near the trees.
A mammal of the dog family, commonly with a pointed muzzle, upright ears, and a bushy tail.
The fox disappeared behind the bushes.
A wild mammal of the dog family, resembling some domestic dogs and often hunting in groups.
A wolf howled in the distance.
Animals usually having feathers, a beak, and a pair of wings, and reproducing by laying eggs. Not all birds can fly.
A small bird landed on the branch.
As a noun, fish names animals that live mainly in water and usually breathe through gills and move with fins. As a verb, it means catching or trying to catch fish.
We watched the fish swimming in the pond.
An insect whose adult usually has two pairs of relatively large wings covered with tiny scales. Its larva is a caterpillar.
A butterfly landed on a flower.
An insect commonly feeding on nectar and pollen. Some species help pollinate plants while gathering food.
A bee flew from flower to flower.
An insect that commonly lives in colonies, with a head, thorax, abdomen, antennae, and six legs.
Ants carried food back to their nest.
An arthropod usually having eight legs, not an insect. Many species produce silk.
In web technology, spider can also mean a program that automatically crawls web pages.
A spider had made a web in the corner.
Reptiles whose bodies are protected by a hard upper and lower shell. Different species live on land, in fresh water, or in the sea.
The turtle pulled its head into its shell.
An amphibian usually tailless as an adult, with long hind legs. Many species jump and reproduce in water.
A frog jumped into the pond.
As a noun, flower is the reproductive structure of a flowering plant, often with petals. As a verb, it means blooming and can figuratively mean developing fully.
The flowers opened in the sunshine.
The plant sense is a perennial plant usually with a woody trunk and branches. In technical contexts, tree can mean a hierarchical branching structure.
The tree gives us shade in summer.
A plant organ that is usually thin and flat. Many leaves produce organic substances through photosynthesis.
The plural is leaves. Leaf can also refer to a page of a book and related meanings.
A leaf fell from the tree.
Rose: a flower or another form of rise
As a noun, rose usually means a plant of the genus Rosa or its flower. Rose can also be the past tense of rise, meaning to go up.
She put a rose in the vase.
A reproductive structure of a plant containing an embryo and protective tissues, capable of developing into a new plant under suitable conditions.
We planted the seeds in small pots.
A plant of the cactus family. Many species have fleshy, water-storing stems and spines and are adapted to dry environments.
The cactus grows slowly in this pot.
Usually the visible fruiting body of certain fungi, often with a stalk and cap. As a verb, mushroom can mean increasing rapidly in number.
Pictures and dictionary descriptions must not be used to decide whether wild fungi are safe to eat.
As furniture, a table has a flat top supported by legs or similar structures. As an information format, it arranges data in rows and columns.
The dishes are on the table.
A chair; to chair a meeting
The noun commonly means a seat for one person, generally with a back. It can also mean the person presiding at a meeting, while the verb means to preside.
She pulled a chair up to the desk.
The noun names a written work presented on pages or electronically. The verb means arranging in advance to reserve a seat, room, or service.
I booked a room for two nights.
A writing or drawing tool, usually with a marking core enclosed in wood or another material. Common pencil cores contain graphite.
He drew a circle with a pencil.
A writing pen; an animal enclosure
The familiar meaning is an ink-writing tool. In animal-keeping contexts, pen can mean a small enclosure.
Please sign your name with a pen.
An implement with a shallow bowl at the end of a handle, commonly used for scooping, stirring, or eating.
Use a spoon to stir the soup.
As tableware, a plate is a relatively shallow object for holding food. It can also mean a flat sheet, board, or particular component.
Put the bread on a plate.
A container for heating water, usually with a handle and spout, heated on a stove or electrically.
The water in the kettle is boiling.
A container usually with a narrow opening, used for water, drinks, or other contents and often made of glass or plastic.
She filled the bottle with water.
A small container for drinks, often with a handle. Cup can also be a unit of volume in cooking and other contexts.
He poured tea into a cup.
An opening and closing device with a covering and frame that protects from rain or sunlight. It can also figuratively mean overall coverage or protection.
She opened her umbrella when it began to rain.
A device for displaying or measuring time, commonly using hands or a digital display.
A timepiece worn on the wrist is normally called a watch.
The clock on the wall shows nine o'clock.
A cutting tool with two crossing blades pivoting around a joint, used to cut paper, cloth, and other materials.
Normally say a pair of scissors; do not treat scissors as an ordinary singular tool noun.
I need scissors to cut this paper.
A bag carried on the back using shoulder straps, often holding books, clothes, or travel supplies.
He put his lunch in his backpack.
A tool for climbing up or down, usually consisting of two side rails joined by rungs.
The worker climbed the ladder carefully.
The noun names a tool with a handle and a heavy head, often used to strike or drive nails. The verb means striking with a hammer or in a similar way.
She used a hammer to drive in the nail.
An instrument collecting and focusing light or other radiation to observe distant objects. Everyday usage often means an optical telescope.
We looked at the moon through a telescope.
An instrument that magnifies details of tiny objects so they can be observed, allowing study of structures difficult to see with the unaided eye.
The cells can be seen under a microscope.
A compass is an instrument for finding direction. In drawing, compasses are an instrument for drawing circles.
A source of light consisting of combustible material and a wick, producing light through burning near the wick.
They lit a candle on the table.
A circular component turning around an axle, commonly used to move vehicles or transmit motion.
One wheel of the cart is broken.
A vehicle usually with two wheels, driven by the rider's pedals, with variants such as electrically assisted bicycles.
She rides a bicycle to work.
A keyboard instrument whose keys activate hammers that strike strings inside, usually with alternating black and white keys.
As a musical direction, piano also means softly.
He practices the piano every evening.
A string instrument commonly held near the shoulder, usually with four strings and played mainly with a bow, though it can also be plucked.
She played the violin in the orchestra.
The noun commonly means connected vehicles running on tracks. The verb means developing an ability through practice or instruction.
The train arrived at the station.
In transport, a bus carries multiple passengers along a route or service arrangement. In computing, a bus is a channel for transferring data.
We took the bus to the museum.
A device recording images through optics and light-sensitive processes, capable of taking still photographs or moving video.
She took a photo with her camera.
An electronic device that processes, stores, and transmits information according to instructions, used for calculation, writing, communication, and other tasks.
The computer saves the file automatically.
In computing, an arrangement of keys for entering text and commands. In music, keyboard refers to the keys of an instrument.
Type your name on the keyboard.
A large landform rising substantially above its surroundings, usually with slopes and a summit. Precise height definitions vary by region and context.
Snow covers the top of the mountain.
Water flowing continuously or intermittently in a natural channel, generally from higher ground toward a lake, sea, or another river.
A place where water in a river or similar body suddenly drops from a higher level to a lower one.
We could hear the waterfall from far away.
Land surrounded by water, in an ocean, lake, or river.
They traveled to a small island.
A geological structure in the Earth's crust connected with underground magma, capable of releasing lava, ash, and gases and forming mountains or other landforms.
The volcano has not erupted for many years.
A coloured arc-shaped optical phenomenon produced by sunlight interacting with water droplets in the air.
A rainbow appeared after the shower.
In nature, a cloud is a collection of tiny water droplets or ice crystals suspended in the atmosphere. In computing, it can refer to remote processing and storage services.
Dark clouds gathered above the town.
A large ecological environment dominated by trees and including other plants, animals, and living organisms.
A narrow path leads into the forest.
The noun usually names a dry region with very little rainfall, not necessarily a place full of sand dunes. The verb separately means abandoning.
The noun and verb usually have different stress patterns.
Some plants can survive in the desert.
A strip along an ocean, lake, or river formed by deposits of sand, pebbles, or similar material.
The vast body of salt water covering most of the Earth's surface, or one of its major named divisions.
The Moon commonly names Earth's natural satellite. A moon can also be a natural satellite orbiting another planet or similar body.
The moon was bright that night.
The Sun is the star at the centre of the Solar System. Its light and heat are important sources of energy for Earth.
The sun rose above the hills.
The noun commonly means the liquid used for drinking and washing, chemically a substance made of hydrogen and oxygen. The verb means giving water to plants and similar things.
Please water the plants this evening.
A drink usually made from roasted, ground coffee seeds and water. Coffee can also mean the beans or ground material.
She drinks a cup of coffee in the morning.
The noun commonly names a building for people to live in. The verb can mean providing accommodation or placing objects or facilities in a building.
The noun names liquid water drops falling from clouds to the ground. The verb means that rain is falling.
The noun names solid precipitation formed from ice crystals, or snow lying on the ground. The verb means that snow is falling.
The noun names a still image recorded through an imaging process using light. The verb means taking photographs.
A person who takes photographs professionally, skilfully, or as a hobby.
The photographer waited for better light.
The technique, activity, or art of recording still images using a camera or similar device; it can also refer to photographic work in a particular style.
Relating to photography, taking pictures, or photographs; used to describe equipment, materials, or image characteristics.
A device converting sound into electrical or other processable signals, used in amplification, recording, and communication.
The noun names a device or system allowing people at a distance to communicate by voice. The verb means calling someone by telephone.
Describes something too small to see clearly without a microscope, or something relating to microscopes.
A water-filled container for keeping or displaying aquatic life, or a public building where aquatic animals and other organisms can be viewed.
The children watched the fish in the aquarium.
Describes organisms living or growing in water, or activities taking place on or in water.
A channel or engineered structure carrying water from one place to another, sometimes built like a bridge over low ground.
The aqueduct carried water to the town.
The process by which plants, algae, and certain bacteria use light energy to make organic substances. Familiar green plants use water and carbon dioxide and release oxygen.
The art and practice of designing buildings, or a style of building. In technical contexts, architecture means the organization of a system's parts.
The city is famous for its modern architecture.
To organize materials, parts, or ideas into a planned whole, such as a building, machine, argument, or model.
They plan to construct a new bridge.
The process of building or assembling, or a completed structure. In linguistics, it can mean a particular combination of words.
Construction of the school starts next month.
The arrangement, connections, and relationships among parts of a whole, or an entity having such an organization, such as a building.
We studied the structure of the bridge.
The activity or system of moving people or goods from one place to another, by road, rail, sea, air, or another means.
Trucks transport food to the city.
The activities, vehicles, and systems used to move people or goods between places.
In computing, an electronic component executing instructions and processing data. Elsewhere, it can mean equipment or an organization processing materials.
The new processor uses less power.
The noun names a vessel capable of travelling underwater. The adjective means situated or occurring below the sea's surface.
The submarine traveled below the surface.
A place for aircraft to take off and land and for handling passengers, cargo, and aviation operations.
We arrived at the airport early.
An instrument measuring temperature, using principles such as liquid expansion or electrical changes.
Use a thermometer to check the temperature.
The noun names a document or image reproduced by copying equipment. The verb means making such a copy.
Please make a photocopy of this page.
Turning around a centre or axis, or people, duties, or activities taking turns in a sequence.
The rotation of the wheel was slow.

Success is related to Latin successus, progress or outcome. It first emphasized the result of events and later commonly a favourable result, success.
Success is a noun naming achievement. Connect it with succeed, to achieve or take over, and successful, an adjective.
Successful is formed from success and the adjective suffix -ful, meaning achieving success or producing a good result.
Success is a noun; successful is an adjective. The project was successful describes the project's outcome.
Successfully adds the adverb suffix -ly to successful, meaning in a successful or smooth manner.
Successful describes a thing; successfully modifies an action. She successfully completed the task describes how it was completed.
Succeed goes back to Latin succedere, to come after or take over. It also developed the common sense of achieving a goal.
Compare succeed in doing something, achieve it, with succeed someone, take over that person's position.
Successor belongs to the succeed family and names someone taking over another person's position or status.
A successor is the person who follows in a position; compare predecessor, the previous holder.
Succession is related to succeed and successor and emphasizes one following another, including a sequence or inheritance of a position.
A succession of events is a series of events; a succession plan prepares for someone to take over a role.
Successive belongs to the sequence-related branch of succession and describes things occurring one immediately after another.
Successive days are consecutive days. Do not confuse successive with successful.
Process is related to Latin processus, advancement or going forward, and developed senses of development and step-by-step activity.
Process emphasizes an activity unfolding, as in a learning process or manufacturing process.
Proceed comes from Latin procedere, to go forward, combining pro-, forward, with cedere, to go. It commonly means continuing.
Proceed with the plan means continue carrying it out. Connect pro- with forward and ced or ceed with going.

Procedure entered English through French procédure, related to procéder and Latin procedere, to proceed. Pro-, forward, ced, going, and the noun ending -ure provide a learning analysis of a prescribed method or procedure.
Imagine completing a task step by step. The prescribed sequence is a procedure.
Procession is related to Latin processio, going forward, and commonly names an organized line of people moving forward.
A procession emphasizes people advancing in a line, as in a wedding procession.
Access is related to Latin accedere, to approach, and developed senses of entry, reaching, and the right to use something.
Access to information is the ability or means to obtain it. Have access to means being able to enter or use something.
Accessible belongs to the access family and describes something reachable, obtainable, or easy to understand.
An accessible website is easy to access; an accessible explanation is easy to understand.
Recede comes from Latin recedere, to go back or withdraw. Re- suggests back and ced or cede going.
Recede can describe retreating water, a moving-back hairline, or something growing more distant.
Recession is related to Latin recessio, retreat or withdrawal. In modern economics it describes a decline in economic activity.
An economic recession is an economic downturn. Connect it with recede, to move back.
Concede is related to Latin concedere, to yield, grant, or agree, and commonly means acknowledging a point or giving way.
Concede a point means acknowledge it; concede defeat means admit that one has lost.
Concession belongs to the yielding or granting family of concede. It can mean a compromise, a special allowance, or an operating right.
Make a concession means yield a point or condition. A concession agreement may grant operating rights.
Precede comes from Latin praecedere, to go before, combining prae-, before, and cedere, to go. It commonly means happening before something else.
A precedes B means A comes before B. Precedence is the related noun for priority or coming first.
Precedent is related to precede and names an earlier example that can guide later events, including in law.
Set a precedent means establish a prior example. A legal precedent is an earlier legal decision used as guidance.
Excess is related to Latin excedere, to go beyond a boundary, and means an amount beyond a normal or proper limit.
In excess of means more than; excess capacity means capacity beyond what is needed.
Excessive is formed from excess and the adjective suffix -ive, meaning beyond a reasonable limit.
Excessive spending and excessive pressure both describe amounts beyond what is normal or appropriate.
